Messages.Author: Lönkka
Messages.Body:
> Adonai wrote:
> In 2011, National Championship organizer's don't automatically qualify.
> The rules might change for 2012.
>
Hear hear!

I recall the autoqualification for ECQ organizers being justified due to plenty of work included in organizing such an event.

Yet some of ECQs are really not that large tournaments. Then you have Nationals where you get some 50 players or so and no autoqualification. Seems kinda unfair even if the line has to be drawn somewhere.

Finnish  Politics!

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body: Wasn't it also an argument that if you organized and judged a qualifier, you couldn't actually play in it yourself and thus would not be able to qualify unless you traveled to a different country for their qualifier?

Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
> Izaak wrote:
> Wasn't it also an argument that if you organized and judged a qualifier, you couldn't actually play in it yourself and thus would not be able to qualify unless you traveled to a different country for their qualifier?
>
Yes, but this was changed in 2011 so that Qualifier organizers could drop their "auto-qualify" status and play in their own qualifiers if they used the multi-judge system.

Unfortunately, the page at www.vekn.net/index.php/continental-championships hasn't yet been updated with language stating such.

(I also agree that organizers of ANY event at ANY level should be able to drop their "auto-qualify" status and play in their own qualifiers if they use the multi-judge system, but this has yet to be addressed by the VEKN.)
